guideVersion: Cobb500 Fast Feather Breeder Management Supplement (L-010-01-20 EN)
publicationDateNote: No explicit publication date is printed in the document. The footer print code 'L-010-01-20 EN' follows Cobb's LNNN-NN-YY convention seen across its management guides; the trailing '-20' most plausibly denotes a 2020 print run, but this is read off the code, not an explicit statement of publication date, so publicationDate is left null rather than asserted.
notes: Transcribed from the Cobb500 Fast Feather Breeder Management Supplement's Female Rearing Guide (Dark Out), Female Production Guide, Breeder Performance table, Fertility/Hatchability/Chick Weight table, and Egg Weight and Grading table (Egg Weight column only), plus the Cobb Male Management Supplement's Table 5 (BW/Nutrient/Feed Intake Guide, Rearing) and Table 7 (BW/Nutrient/Feed Intake Guide, Production) -- the Cobb Male line is shared across both Fast Feather and Slow Feather female crosses per that supplement, so identical male values appear in both this profile and its Slow/Fast Feather counterpart. The Open Sided female BW/feed variant published alongside Dark Out in the same tables was intentionally omitted (Dark Out is Cobb's recommended system per the supplement text), matching how the Ross 308 profile omits its out-of-season variant. Egg Grading % breakdown (small/2-yolk/cull/hairline/cracked/floor), Embryo Diagnosis % breakdown (infertile/early/mid/late dead), Standard Fleshing and Pelvic Fat targets, and the Feed Increase Plan for Pullets table were NOT imported -- out of scope for this profile's required metric set, not because they are unreliable. The Male Supplement's Table 2 ('Example of Proper Testicle Development') and Table 6 ('Example of feed allocation...') were excluded because Cobb itself labels them examples, per this project's rule against promoting example/estimate figures into targets. Values are exactly as published; no interpolation, extrapolation, or estimation.

body_weight_g.table: Female Rearing/Production Guide (Dark Out) / BW, Nutrient and Feed Intake Guide for Cobb Male (Rearing/Production)
body_weight_g.sourceColumn: BW (g) [Dark Out variant; Open Sided variant published in same table intentionally omitted, as with the Ross 308 profile's out-of-season variant]

daily_feed_intake_g.table: Female Rearing/Production Guide (Dark Out) / BW, Nutrient and Feed Intake Guide for Cobb Male (Rearing/Production)
daily_feed_intake_g.note: Female weeks 25-27 have no published per-week feed value in this table; the document instead directs readers to a separate 'Feeding into Lay' table keyed by % hen-day production milestones (5/15/25/.../75%), not by week. That table was not imported (wrong axis for an age-indexed series). Feed intake for female weeks 25-27 is therefore absent from this profile, not estimated.

hen_week_production_pct.footnote: Formula box: Total Eggs (%HW) = Total Eggs Produced / Average Number of Hens for the week. This is a hen-week rate (denominator adjusts for mortality during the week), matching the Ross 308 profile's use of this metric code for its 'Hen-Week (%)' column.

hatching_egg_utilization_weekly_pct.footnote: Formula box: Hatching Eggs (%HW) = Total Eggs (%HW) * % HE Weekly, i.e. % HE Weekly is the fraction of total eggs weekly that qualify as hatching eggs (50g minimum, per the Total Eggs / Hatching Eggs per Hen Housed summary footnote).

eggs_per_hen_housed_cumulative.note: Verified cumulative (not weekly): the final tabulated week's value matches 'Total Eggs / Hen Housed' in the Breeder Performance (Top 25% Flocks) summary box for the corresponding depletion age.

hatching_eggs_per_hen_housed_cumulative.footnote: 50g minimum, per the Breeder Performance (Top 25% Flocks) summary box footnote on 'Hatching Eggs / Hen Housed'.

flock_mortality_cumulative_pct.note: Cumulative female flock mortality from housing/light stimulation, as published; no existing metric code in metric_definitions.json covers flock mortality.

fertility_cumulative_pct.note: Cumulative percentages are allowed to rise then decline near end of lay (unlike cumulative counts); this is expected, not a data error.

hatchability_cumulative_pct.note: Cumulative percentages are allowed to rise then decline near end of lay (unlike cumulative counts); this is expected, not a data error.

flock_mortality_cumulative_pct.note: Cumulative mortality is expected to be monotonically non-decreasing.
